entry_state: Bootstrap uncertainty needs an explicit process law and shared fitted draws. Sparse data and failed draws remain unresolved rather than zero. Lifetime payment, one-year development result and insurer risk compensation are different targets.
exit_state: Conditioning on the latest diagonal differs from conditioning on the full observed triangle. Forward moments do not determine a backward law, and reserve errors must subtract reserve estimates rather than ultimate estimates. The published conditional simulation has its own constructed backward model.
findings: The conditioning example gives mean zero and variance 500 with the diagonal fixed, versus mean 10 and variance 400 with the particular history fixed; both are correct for different targets.
The finite backward-law witness gives conditional probabilities 3/7 and 4/7, mean 11/7 and variance 12/49. Dividing by the forward factor instead gives 3/2.
The manuscript distinguishes the paper's conditional limit assumptions from a programmer's convenient positive distribution.

The reserve-centering example gives error 10; subtracting ultimate 120 from reserve 30 gives the wrong negative 90. The source-equation critique is anchored and makes no claim about unavailable execution code. No new defect observed.
